headline: Daily research brief — Tuesday, October 20

items.title: TSLA reports Wednesday: the only watchlist binary within 48h — premium is an avoid
items.detail: Tesla reports Wed Oct 21 after the close. The Oct-23 front-expiry ATM implied volatility sits at 77.7% (closing marks), implying a ±7% three-day move (straddle-derived ±6.48% from live mid-session quotes) against an 8-quarter realized-reaction average of 7.77% — the only watchlist name priced below its own history. The term structure is inverted (56.5% behind the event), so this is pure event premium. Direction is a coin flip historically (4 up / 4 down; last two both negative). Desk rule: premium into this binary is an avoid. META reports the same evening — a same-session QQQ companion for volatility spillover.

items.title: NVDA is the cleanest seller-paid premium read on the board
items.detail: NVDA's front-expiry ATM implied volatility of 36.2% runs roughly 53% above its trailing 20-day realized volatility of 23.7%, and the realized window is not window-contingent — the only clean event-free richness verdict among the six names. There is no earnings event inside the window (NVDA reports Nov 18), so sellers are being paid for near-term volatility with no binary to justify it. SPY is the milder version: 12.0% front IV against 9.0% realized (+33%), also event-free. QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, and TSLA verdicts stay window-contingent (a single day drives over 30% of their realized variance), so no clean call can be made on those. IV rank is unverified for all six names — no free source exposes single-name IV history.

items.title: AAPL's event premium is rich against its own history — the Nov 2 print decides
items.detail: The Nov 6 straddle (first expiry after the Mon Nov 2 print) implies ±5.22% against an 8-quarter realized average of 2.46% — about 2.1× — and six of the last eight prints were down-but-small. Premium is rich on realized history unless the Jul-26 print (−7.35%, the largest in the sample) marks a genuine regime shift in AAPL reactions rather than an outlier. Only subsequent prints will settle that; the Nov 2 release is the test. MSFT's setup is roughly in line (implied ±5.47% vs 7.02% realized for the Wed Oct 28 print), and its Oct-30 IV of 41.0% is the textbook earnings term-structure hump — expected, not 'rich.' AAPL's event date is verified against today's Nasdaq calendar sweep; NVDA's Nov 18 date is carried from yesterday's package.

items.title: Hormuz escalation is the live macro-vol catalyst; diesel, not crude, is the pressure point
items.detail: Mine strikes on Oct 19 hit two supertankers south of the Strait of Hormuz; Gulf crude flows collapsed to a ~8.5M bpd seven-day average from over 20M the week before, LNG transits largely halted, European gas up 10% in two days. Brent holds $110–111 (five-month high). The tightest barrel is diesel: distillates 12% below the five-year average, the IEA accelerating an emergency ~100M-bbl collective release (over 20M bbl of diesel ASAP), and refinery margins doubling — the curve is pricing refined-product scarcity. EIA's weekly report lands Wed 10:30 ET; last week's −8.6M-bbl crude draw was largely supply-side (Hurricane Isaias shut-ins, low imports), so a big draw should not be read as demand strength. Rates frame the spillover: FRED (Oct 19 observations) has the 10Y at 5.15% — off the 5.31% Oct 5 peak but still a growth-multiple headwind — 2s10s flattened to 38bps from 50bps two months ago, and SOFR sits 1bp below fed funds (3.88%), so no funding stress. Calendar risk: analysts flag further escalation into the Nov 3 midterms.

desks.Dividends: Nothing goes ex-dividend in the next four weeks. MSFT goes ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 (declared; first payment of the Sep 15 raise, its 24th consecutive increase) — two days outside the window. AAPL's dividend is undeclared and expected around Nov 9 with its earnings release — UNVERIFIED. No increases, cuts, or specials in window.
desks.Earnings: TSLA Wed Oct 21 after close (implied ±6.48% vs 7.77% realized average); MSFT Wed Oct 28 after close (implied ±5.47% vs 7.02%); AAPL Mon Nov 2 after close (implied ±5.22% vs 2.46%, ~2.1× rich on history). Consensus EPS: TSLA $0.22, MSFT $4.71, AAPL $2.00. META reports the same evening as TSLA, GOOGL the same session as MSFT. Dates verified against today's Nasdaq calendar sweep.
desks.Futures: Hormuz mine strikes (Oct 19) are the live vol catalyst: flows ~8.5M bpd vs 20M+, Brent $110–111, European gas +10% over two days. Diesel is the pressure point (12% below 5Y average; IEA emergency release accelerated). EIA Wed 10:30 ET — expect a supply-side draw, not a demand read. Grains digesting the Oct 9 WASDE (corn stocks +282M bu to 1.849B; Dec corn near $4.80); next WASDE Nov 10 is the next binary. Gold ~$4,144/oz — the safe-haven bid is absent despite the escalation.
desks.Parity: Quiet: no capturable parity or box violations in liquid names. Methodology note: SPY/QQQ fail the naive call-put parity check on 3-DTE chains, but the deviation is a constant parallel shift — an implied-forward signature (~0.14–0.21% above spot), cause UNVERIFIED — so the call-IV-rich appearance is the forward in the marks, not upside-chase positioning. Cboe's BuyWrite index methodology change (last-trade option pricing replacing the 3:45–4:00pm VWAP, effective Oct 15 close) changes index valuation measurement, not parity mechanics.
desks.Premium: NVDA is the clean seller-paid read (front IV 36.2% vs non-contingent 20d realized 23.7%, ~+53%, no event in window); SPY the milder version (+33%, event-free). QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, TSLA stay window-contingent. MSFT Oct-30 41.0% is an earnings hump, not richness. TSLA 77.7% front IV is the Oct-21 binary; desk rule is avoid. IV rank unverified for all six names.
